newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bonds end steady, bills retain slight rally.
newsitem.headline: NZ bonds end steady, bills retain slight rally.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
* NZ debt markets end largely unchanged
* Sept qtr HLFS next item on domestic agenda
New Zealand debt markets ended largely unchanged on Monday, which dealers said was probably a good performance given the market's current illiquidity.

Bond yields ended on Friday's closing levels, while 90-day bills maintained the slight improvement witnessed at the open, to end at 8.93 percent. December futures managed to notch up seven points to 91.55 with 764 contracts traded.

The currency's Trade-Weighted Index climbed 15 points to 67.68. and a 7.5 billion yen samurai on Friday night also helped money market sentiment. Further dual currency issues are expected throughout the week.
Dealers said the bond market was muted and barely traded at all until lunch, after which it had rallied back to its close.
"It got marked higher this morning on the back of U.S. weakness overnight, but really there were no offshore flows. Even domestic investors were sidelined by end-of-month activity," one dealer said.

He said that in the afternoon session traders seemed to take comfort that the Australian market hadn't weakened off, and that spreads to the U.S. were looking healthy despite US$38.5 billion in refunding looming in U.S. Treasuries this week.

"Because we didn't rally last week as much as the U.S. market, there's a little bit of comfort I suppose up our sleeve that we could weather a bit of upside in the U.S. yields over the next few days," he said.
"There hasn't really been any depth to the market at all, so I suppose unchanged on the day is probably as good an outcome as you could expect," one dealer said.
The Reserve Bank was likely to take some comfort from a 0.6 percent fall Valuation New Zealand's house index in the September quarter.

Little news was seen on the domestic agenda until the September quarter Household Labour Force Survey on Friday. Ongoing political coalition negotiations in the quest to form a new government following an inconclusive general election in October were seen bearing little fruit for a few weeks yet.
